career_spells.evidence_note: Corporate-employer role. Telstra's 2010 prospectus says no shareholder controlled it and describes minority Future Fund holdings after privatisation; public-origin history does not make this public employment. Senior title supplies no hours evidence. Delimiter dates corporate-affairs appointment to July 2009 and regulatory-affairs responsibility from September 2010; an official parliamentary witness list independently observes Watts as Telstra Regulatory Manager on 25 March 2011. His current official biography identifies work on the NBN rollout, radio-spectrum auction and distribution, and network-pricing regulation. Retain one employer spell to avoid overlapping role totals. End remains year-only.

research_notes: Seek Mallesons and Telstra employment/CV records establishing individual full-time status, exact appointments and leave; investigate 2007–2008 break and education/employment overlaps before totals.

2026-09-29 initial research checked DFAT's official APH-derived chronology, member biography, 2013 ABC election profile, ACYD 2015 delegate profile and Telstra 2010 ASX prospectus. Targeted full-time and 2009-appointment searches produced no individual contract or hours evidence; similarly named overseas executives and journalists excluded.

First-speech debate page was inspected but returned multiple speakers and no useful employer match. A snippet about qualifying as a lawyer at age 31 was not attributed to Watts. DFAT's linked professional profile did not return content; no restricted material accessed.

Telstra source expressly addresses ownership/control in the employment era; public-sector clients, NBN policy responsibilities and government-relations duties do not make a commercial employee a public servant. Precise legal-employer entity and any intra-group transfer remain follow-up questions.

No four-year plus two-year calculation is made from year-only ranges without hours and transition evidence; missing public employment evidence is not a verified zero. Last follow-up 2026-09-29; blocked status retained pending substantive evidence.

2026-10-02 follow-up: public professional-profile extract, LSE dissertation, Asialink provider biography, contemporary Delimiter chronology and Watts-specific first-speech section checked. Refined Mallesons and Conroy months and Telstra start; recorded September 2008 dissertation milestone and 2017 training. Direct LinkedIn open returned Internal Error and then (999) Unknown Status Code; no restricted material accessed.

Remaining leads: primary Telstra/Mallesons appointment and departure records, individual hours and leave; reconcile Brumby 2008/2009 and Conroy return chronology. First-speech broad ICT experience is not additive paid employment. Melbourne-law research-page Tim Watts and foreign executives lack identity matching and were not adopted. Last follow-up 2026-10-02; research remains blocked, totals null.

2026-10-03 follow-up: official parliamentary committee material independently observes Watts as Telstra Regulatory Manager on 25 March 2011, corroborating the within-employer role progression without establishing its start or end. His current DFAT biography adds substantive technology-policy duties covering the NBN, spectrum allocation and network-pricing regulation. Searches of Telstra, Mallesons and official parliamentary material did not produce individual contract, hours, leave or departure evidence; the 2008/2009 political-staff conflict remains. Material duties and dated-role enrichment only; no full-time duration calculated.

2026-10-04 follow-up: exact-name Mallesons and Telstra role searches returned derivative biographies and a secondary 15July2009 Telstra appointment report already reflected through the July2009 boundary. No employer personnel record, practising-certificate history, departure day, hours, leave or evidence resolving the 2008/2009 Brumby conflict surfaced. Generic web search is exhausted for this pass; Mallesons/Telstra personnel files and ministerial-office appointment records remain decisive. No substantive fact changed.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Primary publisher records establish previously unrecorded coauthorship of Two Futures and authorship of The Golden Country. Paperback publication milestones12August2015 and17September2019 are kept in evidence notes, not work endpoints; royalties, writing hours and contracts remain unknown. Targeted Mallesons full-time search returned a different delegate’s employment, and Harvard search returned another professional’s study; neither attributed to Watts. Existing commercial employment and political-staff chronology conflicts retained. Next: author contracts if legitimately public, personnel and education records for existing gaps.

Follow-up 2026-10-05: Targeted Bond alumni, Monash public-policy, legal-admission and Telstra departure/leave searches found no individual appointment, conferral, hours or leave record. Monash alumni account of Two Futures concerns policy adviser Matthew, not Watts; Bond Don Watts family biographies concern a different Timothy; performing-arts Tim Watts also rejected. Existing LSE September2008 submission and Telstra month boundary preserved. Current government/party biographies repeat known roles; ten-year technology narrative is not continuous corporate full-time work. Author credits and publisher milestones already recorded; contracts/royalties still unavailable. No substantive fact changed; next useful evidence remains original personnel and ministerial appointment instruments, rather than repeating generic biography searches.
